exercises.title: True versus floor division
exercises.prompt: Predict both lines exactly. Python has no integer division trap the way C does.
exercises.code:
a = 7
b = 2
print(a / b)
print(a // b)

exercises.title: Mean of an empty list
exercises.prompt: This crashes with ZeroDivisionError. Make it print 0.0 for an empty list and still print 2.5 for [1, 4].

exercises.title: One number too many
exercises.prompt: It prints 6 instead of 5. Fix the range.

exercises.title: Why elif
exercises.prompt: Explain what this prints for score=85, and explain why writing 'else if' instead of 'elif' is a habit from another language rather than an improvement.
rubric: explains only the first true branch runs
mentions elif is the Python spelling

exercises.title: The default that accumulates
exercises.prompt: Calling collect twice gives ['a', 'b'] instead of ['a'] then ['b']. Fix it so each call starts empty.
exercises.code:
def collect(item, bucket=[]):
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket

print(collect('a'))
print(collect('b'))
exercises.starter_code:
def collect(item, bucket=None):
    if bucket is None:
        bucket = []
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket

print(collect('a'))
print(collect('b'))

exercises.title: String sort
exercises.prompt: It prints [10, 100, 9]. Make it print the numbers in ascending order without mutating the original list.

exercises.title: KeyError
exercises.prompt: For a missing name this crashes. Make it print 'unknown' instead, without hiding a genuinely wrong value.

exercises.title: The silent failure
exercises.prompt: Nothing is printed and no error surfaces. Make it report the invalid input instead of swallowing it.
exercises.expected_stdout: rejected: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'nope'

exercises.title: State shared between objects
exercises.prompt: Two counters share one total. Make each object keep its own count, so this prints 1 and then 1.

exercises.title: A function worth testing
exercises.prompt: Write clamp(value, low, high) returning value limited to that range. It must print 5, 0 and 10 for clamp(5,0,10), clamp(-3,0,10) and clamp(99,0,10).
exercises.code:
def clamp(value, low, high):
    # return value limited to [low, high]

print(clamp(5, 0, 10))
print(clamp(-3, 0, 10))
print(clamp(99, 0, 10))

exercises.prompt: For a missing file this crashes with FileNotFoundError. Make it print 'no journal yet' instead.

projects.title: CLI Budget & Expense Tracker
projects.purpose: Master Python file I/O, CSV parsing, dictionary aggregations, and robust error handling.

milestones.title: Record an expense entry
milestones.requirements: Prompt user for category, amount (float), and description. Validate non-negative numbers and non-empty strings.
acceptance_criteria: Validates numeric input and handles ValueError cleanly
Stores records in memory as list of dicts
Re-prompts gracefully on invalid data
milestones.hint: Wrap float(input()) in a try/except ValueError block.

milestones.title: CSV persistence & loading
milestones.requirements: Persist expenses into expenses.csv with headers, and load previous records on startup using pathlib or csv module.
acceptance_criteria: Correctly writes headers on first run
Handles missing file without crashing
Data round-trips without data corruption
milestones.hint: Use Path("expenses.csv").exists() and with open(..., mode="a") as f: context managers.

milestones.title: Category aggregation & summary
milestones.requirements: Provide a summary report showing total spent and breakdown grouped by category.
acceptance_criteria: Computes accurate sum per category
Formats currencies cleanly to 2 decimal places
Handles empty logs gracefully
milestones.hint: Use a dict or collections.defaultdict(float) to accumulate sums.

extensions: Export summary report to JSON format

projects.title: Task Management REST CLI & SQLite Engine
projects.purpose: Build an intermediate multi-tier task manager with SQLite persistence, OOP entities, and input validation.

milestones.title: Task domain model & validation
milestones.requirements: Design a Task class with id, title, priority (LOW, MED, HIGH), and status (PENDING, DONE). Reject empty titles.
acceptance_criteria: Constructor validates title and priority constraints
Provides to_dict() and from_dict() serialization methods
Encapsulates status transitions cleanly
milestones.hint: Use an enum for Priority and raise ValueError on invalid state.

milestones.title: SQLite repository layer
milestones.requirements: Create a TaskRepository using sqlite3 context managers to execute schema migration and CRUD operations.
acceptance_criteria: Creates tasks table IF NOT EXISTS on initialize
Parameterized queries prevent SQL injection
Functions return Task object instances
milestones.hint: Always pass parameters as a tuple into cursor.execute(query, params).

milestones.title: Interactive CLI interface
milestones.requirements: Implement add, list, complete, and delete commands with formatted ASCII tabular output.
acceptance_criteria: List command supports filtering by status
Completing non-existent id produces user-friendly error
Formatted output aligns columns neatly

extensions: Add search by title keyword substring
Support due dates with datetime validation
Write automated unit tests using pytest

projects.title: Markdown-to-HTML AST Parser & Static Site Generator
projects.purpose: Advance to compiler and AST concepts: tokenize text, construct block ASTs, and render semantic HTML.

milestones.title: Block tokenizer & lexer
milestones.requirements: Scan lines and categorize into BlockType (HEADING, PARAGRAPH, CODE_BLOCK, LIST_ITEM).
acceptance_criteria: Detects headings (# to ######) with correct levels
Handles multi-line fenced code blocks ``` correctly
Preserves indentation and skips trailing empty lines
milestones.hint: Process lines with a state machine checking if inside_code_block is True.

milestones.title: Inline token parsing
milestones.requirements: Parse inline formatting for bold (**text**), italic (*text*), backtick code (`code`), and links [text](url).
acceptance_criteria: Replaces markdown syntax with <strong>, <em>, <code>, <a>
Escapes special HTML characters (&, <, >) to avoid XSS
Handles nested or adjacent inline tags properly
milestones.hint: Use re.sub with regex capture groups or a character-by-character scanner.

milestones.title: Full document rendering pipeline
milestones.requirements: Combine parsed blocks and inline tokens into complete HTML document wrapped with template layout.
acceptance_criteria: Renders valid, well-formed HTML tags
Writes output file to disk via CLI argument
Achieves 100% test coverage on sample markdown files
milestones.hint: Define a Document.render() method that iterates through blocks and wraps with <!DOCTYPE html>.

extensions: Generate automatic Table of Contents with anchor slugs
Add syntax highlighting classes to code fences
